answer.rationale: Memory_c2 documents that a prior switch to the low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply and that onboarding was quick and invoicing accurate. In contrast, memory_c1 (incumbent renewal stability) now collides with an incumbent that refuses to reopen price under an 18% mandate, and memory_c6 (multi-year leverage) is unavailable this cycle since the incumbent won't renegotiate. Memory_c3 (second-sourcing) is a risk mitigator but adds cost, conflicting with the mandate and with the one-decision constraint. The 14-day expiry and no auto-renew clause force action now; defer_decision is not viable. The 94% line utilization with no buffer is the key delivery-risk flag, so the switch is scoped as a guarded test: transition the primary supply contract to the low-cost vendor whose quote alone meets the 18% reduction, while keeping the incumbent reachable on month-to-month spot terms (precedent in memory_c5) as a short-term fallback during the onboarding window. Verify memory_c2 before committing because the onboarding-speed and invoicing-accuracy claims are the load-bearing assumptions that determine whether delivery risk stays flat during the transition. If the archive contradicts c2 (e.g., onboarding took longer than recalled), fall back to renew_incumbent at current price and absorb the budget variance into the next cycle rather than risk the assembly line.
